script:
Shi Yanren
More than ten years ago, Shi Yankong and Shi Yanren entered Fengbo Temple at the same time. Yankong was much smarter than Yanren and eventually obtained the position of abbot.
After the old abbot passed away, Yankong's behavior changed completely, vigorously using Buddhist convenience to accumulate wealth. This greatly troubled Yanren. But Yankong said he didn't take a penny of this money for himself, so Yanren could only let him be.
After this, the temple also accepted some disciples, the most intelligent of whom was called Hengming, who was very much like Yankong in his youth. Yankong was very fond of him. But his speech, eyes, and even facial features were too much like the young Yankong, which made Yanren somewhat uncomfortable, fearing he would become the next Yankong.
Yankong built a residential area in Fengbo Temple called Quchenju for lay men and women who yearned for Buddhism to stay temporarily for practice and worship. These lay disciples often sought Buddhist teachings from Yanren, among whom a female disciple named Li Xinyue came quite frequently.
A year ago, a special person suddenly came to the temple - a well-known local investor named Zhao Zhengwei. After he came, he only lived in Quchenju. Yanren found it strange why such a person would come to live in Buddhism.
On the evening of July 24th, Yanren came to Yankong's residence and heard loud arguing inside about completely commercializing the temple and fighting over profit distribution. Yanren was furious and forcefully pushed open the door. Inside were Yankong and Zhao Zhengwei, both startled. Yanren scolded Yankong, but Yankong didn't respond much, only saying he would explain when there was a chance.
Heartbroken, Yanren went to the back garden to clear his mind and met Li Xinyue, who was also in the back garden. Li Xinyue came over to talk with him. Yanren poured out his troubles to Li Xinyue, and she used Zen principles to comfort him, making Yanren feel much better. They sat and discussed philosophy, talking until late at night before returning to their rooms to rest.
On July 26th, two days later, Yankong invited Yanren to his room. When Yanren arrived, he found Zhao Zhengwei, Li Xinyue, and another female lay disciple named Zhang Qingzhu all there. Yankong told him to listen to worldly people's voices to understand why he did what he did.
But Yanren believed Buddhist temples should be places of practice - how could they go along with worldly corruption? After persuasion proved fruitless, Yankong had to give up. Zhang Qingzhu left first, and the remaining people ate vegetarian food together. But halfway through the meal, Yanren felt dizzy and feverish all over. Before he could understand what was happening, he lost consciousness.
When he woke up, Yanren found himself lying naked on the bed with a woman beside him - Li Xinyue. Yanren knew what had happened and immediately cried bitterly, because this was equivalent to destroying his lifelong faith. Li Xinyue also woke up and told him she had actually fallen in love with him long ago. But how could Yanren accept such a thing? He hastily put on his clothes and ran back to his own room, no matter how Li Xinyue called after him.
After returning to his room, before Yanren could settle accounts with Yankong, Yankong came to him himself, telling Yanren that since he didn't know what was good for him, they had to use these methods. He told him to keep his mouth shut, and naturally Yankong wouldn't tell anyone about his breaking his vows. Then he left. Seeing his former brother monk become like this, Yanren was in great pain. He even thought of killing Yankong in revenge, but how could he overcome his devotion to Buddhist teachings? He could only calm his mind by constantly practicing calligraphy.
[August 3rd Morning]
At 4:30 this morning, Yanren washed up as usual and went out to prepare for morning prayers in the prayer hall. When he passed by Yankong's room, he met Hengming, who was sneaking around and peeking into Yankong's room. Yanren went over to call him, startling Hengming. Hengming said he was just coming to call Yankong for morning prayers, then hurriedly left. Yanren found it strange - Yankong had never missed morning prayers and always got up on his own. When had he ever needed someone to call him?
At 5 o'clock, after all the monks gathered in the prayer hall, Yankong came to the abbot's seat, picked up the wooden fish mallet and prayer beads, and began leading everyone in chanting. But after just a short while, Yankong's voice suddenly stopped, his whole body convulsed, his face turned purple, he foamed at the mouth, and collapsed to the ground. When Yanren rushed to Yankong's side, Yankong had already stopped breathing.
acts_goal: Do not proactively reveal that Zhao Zhengwei and Yankong had a big fight over unequal profit distribution.
